overview_description: Manage time periods in Exsited: list, create, retrieve, update, enable, disable and delete them.
intro: Time periods define a length of time, such as one month, in your Exsited settings. You can list, create, retrieve, update and delete them, and enable or disable one through its `status`. This area has 5 endpoints, each available in all seven SDKs.
warning: **Deleting a time period cannot be undone.** After a delete, reading the time period returns `404`.
notes: **Request bodies go under `time_period`.** Both the create and the update wrap their fields in a `time_period` object, and every single-record response returns it under `time_period`.
**`period` goes in upper case and comes back in lower case.** Send `MONTHLY`; the response shows `monthly`.
**Time period ids start with `tp_`.** Pass that `id` as `time_period_id`.
**`status` takes `active` or `inactive`.** Send it in an update to enable or disable a time period.

endpoints.title: List time periods
endpoints.summary: Lists the time periods set up in Exsited, one page at a time.
endpoints.description: Returns one page of time periods under `data`, with `pagination` for the next page. Each time period carries its `name`, `display_name`, `period` (such as `monthly`), `duration` and `status`. Any other field of the record filters the listing as `filter_<field>` or `filter_<field>_<operator>`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many records to return on one page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page, to fetch the page after it.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by; prefix it with `-` for descending order, such as `-created_on`.

endpoints.title: Create a time period
endpoints.summary: Creates a time period, such as one month, and returns it under `time_period`.
endpoints.description: Send the new time period under `time_period` with its `name`, `display_name`, `period` and `duration`. Send `period` in upper case, such as `MONTHLY`; the response returns it in lower case, such as `monthly`. The new time period comes back under `time_period` with its `tp_` id.

period.description: The unit of the period, in upper case, such as `MONTHLY`.

duration.description: How many units of `period` the time period spans.

endpoints.title: Retrieve a time period
endpoints.summary: Retrieves one time period by its `tp_` id.

parameters.name: time_period_id
parameters.description: The time period's `id`, which starts with `tp_`.

404.description: No time period has that `id`, for example because it has been deleted.

endpoints.title: Delete a time period
endpoints.summary: Deletes a time period; the response has no body.
endpoints.description: Deletes the time period with this `id`. A successful delete returns `204` with no body, and reading the time period afterwards returns `404`.

parameters.name: time_period_id
parameters.description: The time period's `id`, which starts with `tp_`.

204.description: The time period is deleted. No body.

endpoints.title: Update a time period
endpoints.summary: Updates a time period's details, or enables or disables it.
endpoints.description: Send the fields to change under `time_period`, such as `display_name` or `description`. To enable or disable the time period, send `status` as `active` or `inactive`. The updated time period comes back under `time_period`.

parameters.name: time_period_id
parameters.description: The time period's `id`, which starts with `tp_`.

limit.description: The page size applied to this page.

has_more.description: Whether another page follows. Rely on this rather than on `next_cursor`, which can still hold a value on the last page.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page.
